verdictSummary: The candidate is close. Its type grammar, presence/nullability, ByteString mapping, selectors, namespaces, 13 successor rows and field coverage are concrete and mostly owner-backed. It is not yet sufficient as the single reviewable input for a shared bytes-aware Rust/TS generator plus handwritten admission, for six reasons. (1) The checker cannot run from the 18 frozen files plus the pinned architecture. (2) The transitive executable/data pins are incomplete. (3) The PreparedOutput row bounds widen a retained limit and assign a host-invariant fate to a reachable input. (4) The ProviderFault phase and nullability rule cannot be satisfied by a conforming worker under lawful P3 interleavings. (5) Rust3CanonicalPath does not implement the rust2 rule it cites. (6) The packageKey grammar, bounds and order rest on an assumption that the owner schemas do not guarantee. Each has a scoped concrete fix below; none needs a wire change.

sufficiencyForGeneratorAndAdmission.sufficientAfterRequiredFindings: yes for generator carrier derivation (records, variants, bytes, nullable/optional, externs, frame-payload selectors); handwritten admission additionally needs executable vectors for the prose rules listed in ADV-2
sufficiencyForGeneratorAndAdmission.notClaimed: The IDL is not yet generator input that has been implemented; no generator run, product decoder, admission or compiler, and no M2/M3 qualification was performed or is implied.

authorChoices.choice: PreparedOutput row bounds (macro-expansion <= maxExpansionRows, generated-file <= maxGeneratedFileRows, build-script-directives <= maxPreparedOutputEntries; manifest over frame limit = no spawn, operational-failed/ILLEGAL_STATE)
P3-25 guard outputSeen=false (reset at Analyze, set by FactBatch/CoverageV3); host never sends Cancel before Hello
authorChoices.assessment: ACCEPTED. rust2 T019 guards on stageIndex==0 AND outputSeen==false, and T017/T018 set outputSeen on every Coverage. Stage advance therefore implies outputSeen, and the single outputSeen guard is equivalent. The published P3 table alone admits FactBatch then Unavailable (reviewer trace P3-23,P3-25 through native_evidence_model.v2.protocol3_run), so the overlay is necessary. TS2 T2-14 already carries the guard. Cancel in START: P3-29 *PRE_COMPLETE excludes START. Hello is host-to-worker, so START is host-controlled, and terminating the child without a frame keeps interrupted/130 (native-evidence.md:3838-3843). Advisories ADV-5 and ADV-11 apply.

authorChoices.choice: ProviderFault.phase = host phase at fault receipt; Cancelled.observedPhase = host phase at Cancel send; executionId/analysisOrdinal nullability
authorChoices.assessment: SPLIT. Cancelled.observedPhase ACCEPTED: in every non-faulting trace no worker frame is in flight when Cancel is sent, because P3-29 moves to WAIT_CANCELLED, where any non-Cancelled worker frame is P3-34 (reviewer trace ...P3-29,P3-34). The host send phase therefore equals the worker receipt phase that rust2 names. ProviderFault.phase and its nullability are REJECTED; see RF-4.

authorChoices.choice: Ts2ExecutionIdText ^exec1_[0-9a-f]{32} end-anchored; Ts2ProjectPath 1..4096 scalars; Rust3CanonicalPath <= 4096 UTF-8 bytes
authorChoices.assessment: ACCEPTED as bounds. exec1 grammar: identity-and-evidence.md:63-70 declares the end-anchored product successor grammar, and startup ExecutionIdText is the exact AttemptRecord value, so nothing lawful is refused. TS 4096 scalars: identity-schemas.v3 LogicalPath maxLength 4096 and fact.anchors path maxLength 4096 are JSON Schema scalar counts. Rust 4096 bytes: c2-plan-stage-schema.v3 canonicalRelativePath utf8Bytes max 4096. The Rust3CanonicalPath pattern itself is defective (RF-5), and Ts2SnapshotEntryV1.linkTarget 4096 is a separate unowned bound (ADV-6).

authorChoices.choice: Anchor count 1..100000 enforced at the wire
authorChoices.assessment: ACCEPTED. identity-schemas.v3 fact.anchors maxItems 100000. fact-plane candidateSchema anchors and delivery.v2 FactCandidateV1 anchors state only non-empty. A candidate over 100000 anchors cannot mint fact2, and a worker fault yields no facts either way (native-evidence.md:3838-3843), so the earlier refusal is outcome-equivalent. ADV-8 applies.

requiredFindings.title: PreparedOutput row bounds widen a retained limit and assign a host-invariant fate to a reachable input
requiredFindings.evidence: rust2 PreparedOutputManifestV2.entries is 'length 0..maxPreparedOutputEntries' (rust-provider-protocol.v2.json:385). ProtocolLimitsV3 retains maxPreparedOutputEntries=256 (provider-handshake.schemas.v1.json:340), and §9.3 says all 24 v2 limits are retained with identical values (native-evidence.md:2934). The candidate sets entries maxItems 2000256 and outputOrdinal max 2000255 (wire-carriers.v1.json:2391, :2286). The carrier admits 257 build-script-directives entries (scratch/probe_cbor.out.json), and the only check touching the value is limit-literals, which pins the author's own sum (reviewer mutant m_prepared_total_256). maxExpansionRows/maxGeneratedFileRows (handshake:415; §9.3) are preparation-set limits: no owner makes them per-kind wire limits. At 1,000,000 rows the encoded manifest cannot fit maxFramePayloadBytes (67,108,864), since every entry carries a full PreparedOutputRowV3 with 3 hex bindings, ownerKey and configuration, so those limits are unreachable on the wire. Separately, delivery.v2 overflowFate (delivery.v2.json:998) is justified only because a count <= 128 makes overflow a host defect. An oversized Plan-bound PreparedOutputSetV3 (rows maxItems 1000000, native-evidence.schemas.v2.json:2956) is a reachable user input, so operational-failed/SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE misclassifies it.
requiredFindings.fix: Use the retained total bound: entries maxItems 256 and outputOrdinal max 255, with maxExpansionRows/maxGeneratedFileRows staying set limits. State in PREPARED-V3-SET-JOIN and SUCC-PREPARED-V3 that the host refuses before spawn, as a request precondition, any prepared set that has more than 256 inert rows, whose totalBlobBytes exceed maxPreparedOutputTotalBlobBytes, or whose encoded manifest exceeds maxFramePayloadBytes. Route it like the non-inert/stale prepared refusals in the same D9 row family: request-rejected (2), REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED, a typed detail such as native.prepared-output-exceeds-wire-limit (native-evidence.md:3525). If root instead wants more than 256 rows, it needs an explicit scoped successor for maxPreparedOutputEntries that is jointly satisfiable with maxFramePayloadBytes, for example a paged manifest; this IDL has no such mechanism.

requiredFindings.title: ProviderFault.phase and its null rules are not satisfiable by a conforming worker under lawful P3 interleavings
requiredFindings.evidence: RUST3-FAULT-CANCEL-TYPES (wire-carriers.v1.json:4362) requires phase = 'the host phase in which ... the fault [was] received'. Host-to-worker frames change the P3 phase (for example P3-05 SnapshotManifest, P3-22 Analyze), and P3-28 admits ProviderFault from every *PRE_COMPLETE phase (protocol3-transitions.v1.json:335). The reviewer ran native_evidence_model.v2.protocol3_run on [...,UniverseAccepted, SnapshotManifest, ProviderFault] and on [..., NativeContextVerified, Analyze, ProviderFault]; both are admitted as P3-28 provider-fault (scratch/p3-race.out.json). A worker that faulted before reading the in-flight SnapshotManifest or Analyze can only report READY_SNAPSHOT_MANIFEST or READY_ANALYZE, yet the rule demands RECEIVING_SNAPSHOT or ANALYZING, so a lawful provider fault becomes a protocol violation. The null rules have the same problem. The IDL says 'null iff the worker has not received OpenUniverse/Analyze', which the host cannot observe, while contract.md:221 says 'has not been sent or received', and the two differ. D9 is unaffected, since both routes are operational-failed PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (native-evidence.md:3838-3843), but terminalKind, trace and conformance vectors are nondeterministic. No reviewer mutant of this rule text was caught (m_fault_phase_worker_view).
requiredFindings.fix: Define phase as the worker's phase after the last frame it read or wrote. Host admission: let S be the phases the host has entered since it admitted the last worker-to-host frame (the phase at that admission included, host-to-worker transitions only). Admit phase iff it is in S. For executionId/analysisOrdinal, if OpenUniverse/Analyze was sent after that last admitted worker frame, admit null or the sent value; otherwise require the sent value, or null if never sent. Use the same wording in contract.md §2.8 and SUCC-RUST3-FAULT-CANCEL, and add vectors for the two interleavings above.

requiredFindings.title: Rust3CanonicalPath pattern does not implement the rust2 CanonicalPath rule it cites; pattern dialect undeclared
requiredFindings.evidence:
The note at wire-carriers.v1.json:504 claims the rust2 rule (rust-provider-protocol.v2.json:466: no leading slash, backslash, NUL, drive prefix, empty, dot or dot-dot segment). The pattern at :492 uses '.' inside its lookaheads, and '.' does not match U+000A. Under Python re, which is the checker's engine, and under ECMA-262 without the s flag, the pattern admits 'a
/../b', 'a
//b', 'x
/..' and 'a
/.' (scratch/probe_regex.out.json); every one violates the rule, and the rule does not forbid newline itself. Replacing the pattern with the weaker owner Native2 CanonicalPath (reviewer mutant m_canonical_path_native) is not caught. The owner CanonicalPath (native-evidence.schemas.v2.json:669), used for DependencySourceManifest/Chunk path, has the same newline bypass and additionally admits 'a//b', 'a/' and 'C:x'. The joins to host-constructed manifests currently mask the impact, but a generated validator would encode the wrong language. Across the scalars, 13 patterns use lookahead and Rust3CanonicalPath also uses lookbehind. The Rust regex crate supports neither, and privateRepresentation declares no dialect or lowering.
requiredFindings.fix: Make the segment algorithm normative in handwritten admission: split on '/'; each segment non-empty and not '.' or '..'; no U+0000 or backslash anywhere; not starting with [A-Za-z]:; <= 4096 UTF-8 bytes. Keep the pattern informative. Apply the same rule to DependencySource manifest/chunk paths inside DEPSRC-CUSTODY. Declare in privateRepresentation that patterns are ECMA-262 'u' semantics with (?![\s\S]) meaning end-of-text, and that a generator lowers any lookaround pattern to a handwritten check (\z anchors in Rust). Add newline vectors.

requiredFindings.title: packageKey grammar, bounds and entry order contradict the owner schemas
requiredFindings.evidence: DependencyPackageSourceV1 allows name <= 256, version <= 256 and sourceId <= 4096 scalars with no character restriction and no sourceId minLength (native-evidence.schemas.v2.json:1573). The constructed key 'name SP version SP sourceId' can therefore reach 4610 scalars, but the registered DependencySourceManifestV3.entries.packageKey maxLength is 4096 (:4125 def). Rust3PackageKey (wire-carriers.v1.json:556) has pattern [^ ]+ [^ ]+ [^ ]*, which admits an empty sourceId, but minScalars 5, which refuses the host-constructible 'a 1 ' (probe). A space in sourceId makes the key unparseable. The order claim (contract.md:143-144) that key bytes order equals packages order (name, version, sourceId) holds only if name and version contain no byte <= 0x20. That is a Cargo convention, not an owner constraint: with name 'a\x01' the key order and tuple order disagree (probe keyVsTupleOrderWithControlByte). Mutants m_package_key_min4 and m_depsrc_order_sequence are not caught.
requiredFindings.fix: (a) Define entries order as the tuple (name bytes, version bytes, sourceId bytes, path bytes), which is exactly packages x-opensip-order then DependencyFileManifestV1 path order (as native_evidence_model.v2.py dependency_source_set_admit sorts), not packageKey bytes. (b) Make packageKey admission an exact echo join to the owning package row, with the pattern informative. (c) Add a scoped successor statement that dependency-source set admission refuses, before Plan binding, a package whose name/version contains a byte <= 0x20 or whose constructed key exceeds 4096. (d) Align minScalars with the sourceId domain: either 4, or state that every carried package has a non-empty sourceId, since path packages are excluded by dependency_source_set_admit.
